entities.name: Epic of Manas
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
The Epic of Manas, an extensive and traditional epic poem of the Kyrgyz people, is regarded as a cornerstone of Kyrgyz cultural identity and dates back to the 19th century, although it is believed to encapsulate historical narratives from the 8th century. This epic not only reflects the socio-political landscape of Central Asia but also serves as a vital cultural artifact that conveys the values, struggles, and aspirations of the Kyrgyz people. Significant figures in the narrative include the hero Manas and his descendants, who symbolize unity and resilience against external threats, notably from neighboring empires such as the Mongols and the Russians.

The narrative of Manas unfolds through a series of heroic feats, battles, and alliances, portraying the Kyrgyz people's interactions with various neighboring cultures. Key events within the epic detail the unification of the Kyrgyz tribes under Manas's leadership, as he leads them to victory against foreign invaders and internal divisions. This unification is celebrated in the tales of the epic, which also incorporates themes of loyalty, honor, and the struggle for autonomy, ultimately culminating in the establishment of a distinct Kyrgyz identity.

The legacy of the Epic of Manas extends far beyond its narrative content; it has profoundly influenced the Kyrgyz language, literature, and national consciousness. Recognized as a national treasure, it has been inscribed on the UNESCO Memory of the World Register, ensuring its preservation and recognition on a global scale. The epic continues to inspire contemporary Kyrgyz artists and is a symbol of cultural pride, serving as a reminder of the resilience of the Kyrgyz people throughout history.

As the poet and scholar Aitmatov noted, 'In every epic, there is a piece of the soul of a nation,' highlighting the profound cultural significance and enduring legacy of the Epic of Manas in shaping not only Kyrgyz identity but also the broader narrative of Central Asian history.

Their legacy is studied through the lens of historical causation.", "summary": "The Epic of Manas (Kyrgyz: Манас дастаны, Manas dastany) is the national epic of the Kyrgyz people — an enormous cycle of oral heroic poetry narrating the life and deeds of the legendary hero Manas, his son Semetei, and his grandson Seitek (the so-called 'Manas trilogy'), performed by specialist bards called Manaschi (singular: Manaschi). The Manas epic is one of the three great epics of the Mongolian/Central Asian world alongside the Tibetan/Mongolian Epic of King Gesar and the Kalmyk Epic of Jangar, and is of extraordinary length — in its extended versions it is estimated at over 500,000 lines (approximately twenty times the length of Homer's Iliad), though the performed versions by different Manaschi vary enormously in scope. The Manas epic was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013.

The Manas epic narrates the legendary history of the Kyrgyz people — their migration, their resistance against the Kalmyk (Oirat) invaders, their search for a homeland, and the deeds of the hero Manas as their supreme military and spiritual leader. The epic's core themes — the unity of the Kyrgyz tribes under a heroic leader, the struggle against enemies threatening the survival of the Kyrgyz nation, and the establishment of the Kyrgyz homeland — gave the epic its extraordinary resonance as the primary vehicle of Kyrgyz national identity, particularly after the Kyrgyz conquest by Russia (1855–1876) and during the Soviet period.

The Manaschi tradition — the specialist bards who memorise and perform the Manas epic — is one of the most distinctive features of Kyrgyz oral epic culture. The great 19th-century Manaschi Sagynbay Orozbakovev and Sayakbai Karalaev are considered the most important performers of the tradition, with Karalaev's version (c. 1920–1970) running to approximately 500,000 lines and constituting the most extensive documented version of the epic. historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Epic of Manas significantly shaped Kyrgyz national identity and cultural pride, influencing literature and arts while promoting unity among the Kyrgyz tribes. Its recognition by UNESCO underscores its importance as a cultural heritage that continues to resonate in contemporary Kyrgyz society.
